name: Deflazacort
sections: White to off-white crystalline powder, practically insoluble in water.

An oxazoline derivative of prednisolone; potency is about 70–90% that of prednisone (6–7.5 mg deflazacort ≈ 5 mg prednisolone). First approval/introduction: Patented 1969; approved 1985 (Lepetit / Gruppo Lepetit, Italy); US FDA 2017 for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.

Inactive prodrug converted to 21-desacetyl deflazacort; binds glucocorticoid receptors to suppress inflammatory gene transcription and immune responses. 6–7.5 mg deflazacort ≈ 5 mg prednisolone; reported to have relatively less effect on bone and glucose metabolism. Receptor / target profile: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist reducing inflammatory gene transcription and immune activity.
Plasma esterases to active 21-desacetyl deflazacort; then CYP3A4
Summary: Rapidly absorbed and converted to active metabolite; Tmax 1–2 h. Metabolised by CYP3A4. Half-life ~1.1–1.9 h (biological effect longer).
Rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile chronic arthritis, polymyalgia rheumatica
Other conditions responsive to systemic glucocorticoids
Adults: acute disorders up to 120 mg/day initially; maintenance usually 3–18 mg/day
Single morning dose; taper gradually after prolonged use
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Osteoporosis, diabetes, hypertension risk – lowest effective dose; calcium/vitamin D.
Growth suppression – monitor height; DMD ≥2 years: 0.9 mg/kg/day.
Use only if clearly needed; risk of fetal growth restriction and neonatal adrenal suppression.
Excreted in milk; caution at high doses.
Systemic fungal infection and untreated systemic infections
Live vaccines in patients on immunosuppressive doses
Adrenal suppression – do not stop abruptly after prolonged use
Infections may be masked or worsened (TB reactivation, varicella)
CYP3A4 inducers (rifampicin, carbamazepine) reduce effect; inhibitors (clarithromycin, ketoconazole) increase it
Take with food; limit salt; ensure calcium intake.
BP, glucose, weight, electrolytes; bone density on long-term use; eye exam; growth in children.
Acute overdose rarely serious; chronic excess causes Cushingoid effects. Supportive care.
Griggs et al., Neurology 2016 – deflazacort improved muscle strength in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
Comparative studies suggest less weight gain and glucose intolerance than prednisolone at equivalent doses.
Take in the morning after breakfast
Do not stop suddenly after long-term use
Carry a steroid card if on long-term therapy
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
